newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Dharmala Sakti steps in.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Dharmala Sakti steps in.

text.p: Asian debt markets continued to meander through a slow Easter holiday week, offering few new issues on Thursday.
Financial markets throughout the region will be closed on Friday to mark Good Friday.
Australia, New Zealand and Hong Kong markets will be closed on Monday as well, while China has a partial market holiday on that day due to Hong Kong's closing.

DSS Overseas International BV, a unit of Indonesian finance company Dharmala Sakti Sejahtera, on Thursday launched a three-year US$100 million floating rate note issue via lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The notes were launched at par to float at 237.5 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return to top tier participants is 261 basis points.
The deal, which is the first issue off the borrower's US$350 million Asian Currency Note programme, was roadshowed in Hong Kong, Singapore, Seoul and Taipei.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell also brought a US$30 million FRN for China Venturetechno International. The notes mature in three years but can be put after two.
They pay a margin of 120 basis ponts over LIBOR and an all-in return of 155 basis points.
The borrower, China Venturetechno International, is wholly owned by China Venture Tech Investment Corp, which in turn is wholly owned by Chinese state corporations.
China Venture Tech Investment Corp is one of 14 non-bank financial institutions to report directly to the Peoples Bank of China.
In the loan markets, Sino Group set a HK$800 million term loan to finance the acquisition of stakes in Hong Kong's Conrad Hotel.
In other news, Thai borrowers appear to be getting back in the bond game.
Bangkok Bank said its shareholders had approved its plan to issue the first US$1.5 billion tranche of a total Us$3.0 billion worth of various types of bonds in foreign currencies.

The first tranche of bonds that received shareholder approval will be issued in various forms, including subordinated and perpetual bonds, Bangkok Bank said in a statement to the Stock Exchange of Thailand.

On Wednesday, Thailand's PTT Exploration said it would seek shareholder approval to issue unsecured debentures worth up to US$200 million in foreign markets, while Thai Petrochemical said that it planned to issue 10-year debentures valued up to US$200 million in foreign currencies.
Syndicate sources in New York told Reuters they expect Thailand's sovereign bond to come in two tranches, a US$500 million 10-year issue and a US$200 million 30-year tranche.
Launch is expected in early April. Lehman Brothers and Salomon Brothers are the leads.
